facts.one_liner: England’s 90,000-seat national stadium—crowned by the 133-metre arch visible across London.
facts.why_go: Today’s Wembley Stadium, opened in 2007 on the site of the old Twin Towers ground, is England’s national stadium and the UK’s largest sports venue, with 90,000 seats. The photo matches the exterior under the world’s longest single-span roof-support arch—133 metres tall and a landmark from much of north-west London. Official stadium tours take visitors behind the scenes on non-event days; the tour entrance is on Level 1 behind the Bobby Moore statue. FA Cup finals, England internationals, NFL games and major concerts still fill the bowl through 2025–2026.
facts.best_time: Clear daylight for arch and bowl exterior photos; weekday non-event mornings for quieter plazas. Check the events calendar before booking a tour—match or show prep can switch you to an Express Tour without player areas.
facts.how_to_get_there: Wembley Park / Olympic Way, HA9 0WS, London. Tube/Overground to Wembley Park (Jubilee/Metropolitan) or Wembley Central (Bakerloo/Overground); follow Olympic Way to the stadium.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN and hosting events and stadium tours through 2025–2026 (official site lists England fixtures and tours into late 2026). Restricted bag policy applies on event days; allow about two hours for a full tour.

facts.one_liner: Montjuïc’s Olympic Stadium—1992 Games host, not Camp Nou—on the Anella Olímpica esplanade.
facts.why_go: Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys (often Estadi Olímpic de Montjuïc) crowns Barcelona’s Olympic Ring on Montjuïc; it staged the athletics and ceremonies of the 1992 Summer Olympics. The photo is an exterior panorama of this venue—not Camp Nou—showing the classic bowl and surrounding Anella Olímpica landscape with Palau Sant Jordi nearby. Visitors enter via the Old Marathon Gate under Pau Gargallo’s equestrian “Genets” sculptures and can see Ramón Bigas’s Olympic cauldron before walking through to the esplanade. FC Barcelona used the stadium as a temporary home while Camp Nou was rebuilt and returned to the renovated Camp Nou in late 2025; the Olympic Stadium itself remains open for visits and events.
facts.best_time: Summer hours (1 Apr–31 Oct) 10:00–19:00 and winter (1 Nov–31 Mar) 10:00–17:00 for the visitor area; esplanade opens earlier. Event/concert set-ups can close access for weeks—check the official visit page before you go.
facts.how_to_get_there: Passeig Olímpic 17/19, 08038 Barcelona (Anella Olímpica, Montjuïc). Metro L1/L3 to Espanya then escalators/bus up Montjuïc, or bus lines serving the Olympic Ring; taxis and rideshares drop at the esplanade.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for public visits 2025–2026 on non-event schedules (official Estadi Olímpic site). Palau Sant Jordi interiors are not on the visit route. Do not confuse with Spotify Camp Nou in Les Corts.

facts.one_liner: Real Madrid’s renovated home—steel-louvre wrap, retractable roof, Tour Bernabéu year-round.
facts.why_go: Estadio Santiago Bernabéu, Real Madrid’s home since 1947, has completed its GMP/L35/Ribas redevelopment: a wraparound stainless-steel façade, large unsupported cornice over the main square, retractable roof, and about 80,242 seats. The photo (December 2024) shows that current street presence—the continuous horizontal steel-louvre skin and overhang that now define the Concha Espina / Castellana exterior. Tour Bernabéu (Gate 84) covers the museum, panoramic bowl views, and usually dressing rooms and dugouts when match ops allow. It remains one of Madrid’s busiest sports landmarks through the 2025–2026 calendar.
facts.best_time: Non-match weekdays for the fullest tour route; Mondays–Saturdays 09:00–19:00 and Sundays/holidays 09:30–18:30 except 25 Dec and 1 Jan. On match days tours typically end 5½ hours before kick-off; dressing rooms/benches close the day before and on match day.
facts.how_to_get_there: Av. de Concha Espina 1, 28036 Madrid. Metro Santiago Bernabéu (L10); buses along Paseo de la Castellana; Cercanías to Nuevos Ministerios then a short walk north.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN daily for Tour Bernabéu 2025–2026 (official Real Madrid / Turismo Madrid). Route and hours can change for events—confirm on realmadrid.com before visiting. Bernabéu Market food hall is reached via Gate 54.

facts.one_liner: Milan’s Giuseppe Meazza—San Siro—red roof beams, helical towers, Museum&Tour at Gate 6.
facts.why_go: Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, universally called San Siro, is Milan’s historic football cathedral shared for decades by AC Milan and Inter. The exterior photo shows the layered rings, spiral access towers and distinctive red roof trusses that define the stadium’s silhouette. Museum&Tour (entrance beside Gate 6) walks dressing rooms, tunnel, pitchside and the San Siro Museum; a seasonal Skywalk follows the red beams high above the stands. The venue remains open for tours and matches in 2025–2026 while city and club plans for a long-term successor continue to evolve.
facts.best_time: Daily Museum&Tour roughly 09:30–18:00 (Apr–Oct) or 09:30–17:00 (Nov–Mar); Skywalk typically March–October, weather permitting. Avoid last-minute match-day closures—check the opening calendar.
facts.how_to_get_there: Piazzale Angelo Moratti, 20151 Milan. Metro M5 to San Siro Stadio; tram/bus to the stadium district. Museum&Tour and Skywalk entry at Gate 6.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for Museum&Tour (and seasonal Skywalk) 2025–2026 via sansirostadium.com. Match/event days change hours and route without much notice; Skywalk has height, footwear and health restrictions.

facts.one_liner: FC Bayern’s Fröttmaning home—Herzog & de Meuron’s illuminated ETFE cushion façade.
facts.why_go: Allianz Arena opened in 2005 in Munich-Fröttmaning as a purpose-built football stadium designed by Herzog & de Meuron. The photo focuses on the exterior detail that made it famous: diamond-shaped air-filled ETFE cushions (officially about 2,874 panels covering the roof and façade) that form a luminous membrane shell, lit in club colours after dark. FC Bayern München owns and plays here; Arena Tours explain the façade and take you through stands, tunnel and pitchside, with the FC Bayern Museum on the same visit. Night matches still turn the shell red for home fixtures through the 2025–2026 seasons.
facts.best_time: Non-match days for Museum + Arena Tour (most days except 25 Dec, 31 Dec, 1 Jan); dusk or night for the LED façade. Book tours online ahead—same-day tickets often sell out.
facts.how_to_get_there: Werner-Heisenberg-Allee 25, 80939 Munich (Fröttmaning). U-Bahn U6 to Fröttmaning, then the pedestrian esplanade to the Arena; parking is extensive but match days are congested.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for FC Bayern Museum and Arena Tours 2025–2026 (allianz-arena.com). Museum hours typically 10:00–18:00; museum renovation windows can temporarily alter the Arena View product—check the ticket shop.

facts.one_liner: Berlin’s colonnaded Olympic Stadium—1936 Games stage, Hertha home, EURO 2024 final venue.
facts.why_go: Olympiastadion Berlin is the monumental stadium at Olympischer Platz, rebuilt for the 1936 Olympic Games and comprehensively renovated with a modern PTFE roof for the 2006 FIFA World Cup. The photo shows the exterior colonnades and massing that still dominate the Olympiapark approach. On non-event days you can walk the stands and grounds with info boards or a multimedia guide, or join guided Highlight tours; Hertha BSC plays Bundesliga here, and the stadium hosted the UEFA EURO 2024 final. Roughly 300,000 sightseeing visitors a year make it one of Berlin’s major sports landmarks.
facts.best_time: Non-event days when the visitor centre lists full opening (often ~09:00–19:00 in season); Fridays/Saturdays may be guided-tours-only in some weeks. Avoid Hertha home matches and major concerts for sightseeing access.
facts.how_to_get_there: Olympischer Platz 3, 14053 Berlin. S-Bahn Olympiastadion (S3/S9) or U-Bahn Olympia-Stadion (U2); follow signs to the visitor centre at the east side.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for sightseeing and guided tours 2025–2026 (olympiastadion.berlin). Last entry usually 30 minutes before closing; visitor centre closes on Hertha home days and major events—confirm hours online.

facts.one_liner: Rio’s Estádio Jornalista Mário Filho—Maracanã—temple of two World Cup finals and Olympics.
facts.why_go: Estádio Jornalista Mário Filho, universally known as Maracanã, is Rio de Janeiro’s most famous football ground and a venue for the 1950 and 2014 FIFA World Cup finals plus the 2016 Olympic football tournament. The exterior photo shows the modern bowl and surrounding complex after post-2014 upgrades along Avenida Rei Pelé. The official Maracanã Tour (~50 minutes) typically includes locker rooms, mixed zone, press areas, historic memorabilia (Pelé, Garrincha, Zico) and pitch access when operations allow. Flamengo, Fluminense and Brazil national-team fixtures still pack the stands in 2025–2026.
facts.best_time: Non-match mornings for the fullest tour (site often lists ~09:00–17:00 with earlier last entry). NFL, derbies and concerts can close the tour for days—always check tourmaracana.com.br before you go.
facts.how_to_get_there: Avenida Rei Pelé, s/n, Maracanã, Rio de Janeiro (tour/parking often via Gate 2). MetrôRio Line 2 to Rei Pelé–Maracanã station; buses and rideshares serve the stadium district.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for matches and the official Tour Maracanã in 2025–2026, with temporary closures for special events (e.g. NFL windows). Bring ID as required for entry; confirm last-entry times on the day.

facts.one_liner: Estadio Banorte in Tlalpan—Mexico City’s World Cup venue, historically Estadio Azteca.
facts.why_go: Estadio Banorte is Mexico City’s landmark football stadium in Tlalpan, known for decades as Estadio Azteca and still remembered under that historic name. After a multi-year renovation—new seating, hybrid pitch, screens, and fan amenities—it reopened in 2026 and is set to host FIFA World Cup 2026 matches (FIFA’s tournament name is Mexico City Stadium / Estadio Ciudad de México). The photo shows the refreshed exterior after reopening. Club América’s historic home remains a major Liga MX and international venue.
facts.best_time: Non-match days for exterior views around Calzada de Tlalpan / Avenida del Imán; World Cup and Liga MX calendars tightly control access in mid-2026—use official stadium and ticket channels.
facts.how_to_get_there: Calzada de Tlalpan 3465, Santa Úrsula Coapa, Tlalpan, Mexico City. Metro Línea 2 to Taxqueña then light rail/bus toward the stadium, or Metrobús/corridors serving southern CDMX; rideshares are common for visitors.
facts.good_to_know: OPERATING after 2026 reopening. Current commercial/official name is Estadio Banorte (estadiobanorte.com.mx); Azteca is the historic alias. During FIFA World Cup 2026 the venue appears as Mexico City Stadium. Confirm match and visit access via stadium and ticket partners.

facts.one_liner: Cubs’ Friendly Confines—red Clark & Addison marquee on the green-steel grandstand, ivy walls, National Historic Landmark.
facts.why_go: Wrigley Field, opened in 1914 as Weeghman Park and home of the Chicago Cubs since 1916, is a National Historic Landmark and the oldest National League ballpark still standing. The photo shows the classic exterior: the iconic red WRIGLEY FIELD HOME OF CHICAGO CUBS marquee on the green-steel grandstand façade above Gate 3, seen from the brick plaza—unmistakably the ballpark rather than a gate-crowd crop. Non-game ballpark tours explore dugouts, clubhouse areas, press levels and the field when operations allow; Gallagher Way on the west side is a public gathering plaza on many dates. The Cubs still play a full MLB schedule here through 2025–2026.
facts.best_time: Daylight for marquee and grandstand exterior photos from the Clark/Addison plaza; non-game-day tours usually offer the deepest access. Game days are atmospheric but crowded—arrive early for a clear exterior shot.
facts.how_to_get_there: 1060 W. Addison St., Chicago, IL 60613 (Clark & Addison). CTA Red Line to Addison; buses along Clark and Addison. Tour meeting points are posted on cubs.com (often Gallagher Way / Clark Street side).
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for MLB games and official tours 2025–2026 (mlb.com/cubs). The marquee-and-grandstand exterior is the classic plaza photo; bag and security rules apply on game days. Confirm tour inventory on the Cubs ballpark tours page.

facts.one_liner: Boston Red Sox home since 1912—Green Monster left-field wall and Fenway bowl under the light towers.
facts.why_go: Fenway Park opened in 1912 and remains the oldest Major League Baseball ballpark still in use, home of the Boston Red Sox. The photo is a wide in-bowl dusk view with the Green Monster left-field wall, diamond, light towers, and packed stands—Fenway’s signature architecture rather than a Jersey Street façade plaque. Official year-round guided tours (about an hour) typically highlight the Green Monster, Pesky’s Pole, press areas and the Living Museum when the route allows. Walking Lansdowne Street behind the Monster and circling Jersey Street still gives the classic exterior circuit even without a ticket.
facts.best_time: Non-game weekdays for calmer exterior photos and fuller tour access; dusk/night games light the Monster and brick façades. Tours often pause or shorten three hours before first pitch on home dates—book ahead in summer.
facts.how_to_get_there: 4 Jersey Street, Boston, MA 02215. MBTA Green Line (B/C/D) to Kenmore or Fenway; walk to Gate D / Team Store area for tours. Limited neighborhood parking—transit is strongly preferred.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for Red Sox games and public tours 2025–2026 (mlb.com/redsox). Exterior is freely viewable from public sidewalks; bag policies and street closures tighten on game days.

facts.one_liner: MSG above Penn Station: Knicks and Rangers home; World’s Most Famous Arena tours.
facts.why_go: Madison Square Garden sits atop Pennsylvania Station at 4 Penn Plaza in Midtown Manhattan—the plaza entrance with the MADISON SQUARE GARDEN marquee and yellow taxis the photo shows. The current Garden (opened 1968) is home to the NBA’s New York Knicks and the NHL’s New York Rangers and hosts concerts, boxing, and special events year-round. Official 60-minute Madison Square Garden Tour Experiences visit backstage areas, a luxury suite, and the Hyundai Bridge view of the concave ceiling; Knicks and Rangers locker rooms are included on non-game days when operations allow.
facts.best_time: Non-event midweek mornings for plaza photos and the best chance of full tour access. Game nights and big concerts fill Seventh Avenue and Penn Station; arrive early or use transit.
facts.how_to_get_there: 4 Pennsylvania Plaza, New York, NY 10001, above Penn Station. Subway A/C/E to 34 St–Penn Station, 1/2/3 to 34 St–Penn Station, or B/D/F/M/N/Q/R/W to 34 St–Herald Square; PATH and NJ Transit/LIRR also terminate under the arena. Tour desk is on Seventh Avenue between W. 31st and W. 33rd Streets.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (official MSG tour calendar and Knicks/Rangers home schedules). This is the fourth Madison Square Garden building—not the 19th-century gardens near Madison Square Park. Security screening is standard; bag rules tighten on event nights.

facts.one_liner: MCG in Yarra Park: AFL Grand Final and cricket colossus; capacity 100,024.
facts.why_go: The Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in Yarra Park, Jolimont, is Australia’s largest stadium—the concrete-and-glass exterior with teal roof trusses and AFL banners shown in the photo. Official capacity is 100,024 (about 95,000 seats plus standing). It hosts AFL home-and-away and finals (including the Grand Final), international and domestic cricket, and occasional special events such as the 2026 NFL Melbourne Game. Guided MCG Tours depart Gate 3 on select days with MCC volunteer guides; the Australian Sports Museum sits under the same roof.
facts.best_time: AFL season (roughly March–September) and summer cricket for atmosphere; non-event weekdays for tours and the museum. Grand Final week and Boxing Day Test are the densest crowds.
facts.how_to_get_there: Yarra Park, Jolimont, VIC 3002. Walk from Jolimont or Richmond stations; tram routes along Wellington Parade / Brunton Avenue. Driving is discouraged on big match days—use public transport.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (MCG 2026 AFL seating maps and Ticketek event calendar live). Book MCG Tours ahead; routes vary with events. Tickets for MCG events are via Ticketek (Ticketmaster only for the listed 2026 NFL fixture).

facts.one_liner: New Zealand’s national stadium in Kingsland; rugby, cricket, concerts; ~50,000.
facts.why_go: Eden Park in Kingsland, Auckland, is New Zealand’s national stadium—the elevated view with EDEN PARK lettering on the façade and the curved South Stand canopy amid suburban streets matches the photo. Official materials call it the only NZ venue able to host about 50,000 for sport (scaling higher for concerts). It stages All Blacks and other rugby Tests, domestic Super Rugby and cricket, football, and live music. Guided Stadium Tours (~90 minutes) run Thursday–Sunday at 14:00 from Entry G on Reimers Avenue when the calendar allows.
facts.best_time: Winter rugby Test windows and summer cricket for match atmosphere; Thursday–Sunday afternoons for public tours on non-event days. Concert and night-game schedules expanded under 2026 planning rule changes—check the events calendar.
facts.how_to_get_there: 42 Reimers Ave, Kingsland, Auckland. Western Line train to Kingsland Station then a short walk; buses serve New North Road / Dominion Road. Tour parking is in Car Park P5 at Gate G off Reimers Avenue.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (edenpark.co.nz tours and August 2026 venue news live). Casual walk-ins inside the bowl are not allowed outside events; book a tour or tickets. Residential surrounds mean strict noise and egress rules on event nights.

facts.one_liner: Ajax’s Amsterdam home; official Johan Cruijff ArenA with retractable roof.
facts.why_go: Johan Cruijff ArenA (official styling) is Ajax’s home on Johan Cruijff Boulevard in Amsterdam Zuidoost—the exterior with the steel retractable-roof lattice and entertainment-plaza setting shown in the photo (Pathé and ArenA Boulevard sit next door). Opened in 1996 as Amsterdam ArenA and renamed for the 2018–19 season after Johan Cruyff, it is the Netherlands’ largest football stadium and also hosts national-team matches and concerts. Classic and guided stadium tours (dressing rooms, tunnel, dugout, Gallery of Fame) run most days from Entrance E beside the Ajax fan shop.
facts.best_time: Non-match weekdays 09:30–16:30 for self-guided Classic tours; European nights and Eredivisie weekends for atmosphere. Summer concert setups can close or alter tour routes.
facts.how_to_get_there: Johan Cruijff Boulevard 1, 1101 AX Amsterdam. Train or metro to Amsterdam Bijlmer ArenA (about a five-minute walk); Strandvliet metro is another option. P+R parking sits under the stadium.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (johancruijffarena.nl lists 2026 Ajax, Oranje, and concert dates). Scout swapped Cape Town Stadium → this venue for Commons FoP. Do not confuse with the older Olympic Stadium (Olympisch Stadion) west of the centre.

facts.one_liner: Kengo Kuma’s Tokyo 2020 stadium in Kasumigaoka; wood eaves by Meiji Gaien.
facts.why_go: Japan National Stadium (国立競技場 / Japan National Stadium) in Kasumigaoka-machi, Shinjuku, is the Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic centrepiece—the layered wooden-louver eaves and landscaped walkway with sakura in the photo. Designed by Kengo Kuma and Associates with Taisei and Azusa Sekkei, it uses timber from all 47 prefectures and sits by the Meiji Jingu Gaien outer gardens. It hosts athletics, football, rugby, and other national events; official stadium tours (observation deck, VIP areas, locker rooms, track) run on scheduled dates via the operator’s booking site.
facts.best_time: Late March–early April for cherry blossom along the approach; clear autumn days for exterior photos. Book tours on published calendar dates—event and works days change access.
facts.how_to_get_there: 10-1 Kasumigaoka-machi, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo. Toei Oedo Line Kokuritsu-Kyogijo Station (about one minute walk), JR Chuo-Sobu Sendagaya Station (~5 minutes), or Ginza Line Gaienmae (~15 minutes).
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (tours and J.League National Stadium Day fixtures listed). Formal name remains Japan National Stadium; commercial call name MUFG Stadium applies 1 Jan 2026–31 Dec 2030 per operator partnership (clean-stadium rules still use the formal name).

facts.one_liner: BVB’s SIGNAL IDUNA PARK (Westfalenstadion): Yellow Wall; 81,365 Bundesliga.
facts.why_go: SIGNAL IDUNA PARK—still widely called Westfalenstadion—is Borussia Dortmund’s home in Dortmund’s west end, with the trademark yellow roof pylons and SIGNAL IDUNA banding the photo captures. Official figures put Bundesliga capacity at 81,365, including 24,454 standing places on the Südtribüne (the Yellow Wall); international fixtures convert standing areas to seats (66,099). BVB stadium tours and the Borusseum museum run on selected non-match days from the official club site.
facts.best_time: Bundesliga home weekends for the Südtribüne roar; weekday mornings for Stadium Walk / guided tours when listed. International match weeks use the reduced all-seater layout.
facts.how_to_get_there: Strobelallee 50, 44139 Dortmund. S-Bahn / regional rail to Dortmund Signal-Iduna-Park or Westfalenhalle area; tram lines serve the stadium district. Follow BVB access maps on matchdays—approach roads close early.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (bvb.de / signal-iduna-park.de capacity and tour pages live). Scout swapped Stade de France → this venue for French FoP limits. Cashless at fixed stands; away fans use northern blocks.

facts.one_liner: Manchester United’s Theatre of Dreams—Old Trafford bowl, white roof trusses, and East Stand façade.
facts.why_go: Old Trafford in Trafford, Greater Manchester, is Manchester United’s home ground—the photo is an aerial of the stadium itself, with the red seating bowl, pitch, white cantilever roof trusses, and exterior WELCOME TO OLD TRAFFORD / THEATRE OF DREAMS branding. Official Old Trafford Tour & Museum visits (~70 minutes plus museum floors) cover dressing rooms, the players’ tunnel, pitchside dugouts, and the press area on non-home-match days. Sir Matt Busby Way and the East Stand forecourt remain the classic street-level approach for matchday atmosphere and exterior photos.
facts.best_time: Sunday–Thursday openings are shorter than Friday–Saturday; avoid home matchdays when tours and museum close. Clear daylight shows the roof lattice and bowl best from the Trafford side approaches.
facts.how_to_get_there: Sir Matt Busby Way, Old Trafford, Manchester M16 0RA. Metrolink to Old Trafford or Wharfside; National Rail to Manchester United Football Ground on matchdays. Tour parking guidance uses postcode M16 0SZ (E2 car park when open).
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (manutd.com Tour & Museum hours and booking live). Tours start from Sir Alex Ferguson Stand reception; allow time for bag checks. Fixture changes can cancel tour days—check confirmation email. The United Trinity statue on the East Stand forecourt is a separate street-level stop, not the hero view.

facts.one_liner: Liverpool FC’s Anfield—full red bowl, The Kop’s L.F.C. seats, and Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand.
facts.why_go: Anfield in Liverpool’s Anfield district is Liverpool FC’s home—the photo is a fuller interior bowl panorama from the Main Stand side, with red seating, The Kop’s L.F.C. lettering, Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand fascia, and the pitch (not a street-level Kop/Paisley Gateway crop). Guided LFC Stadium Tours & Museum visit the This Is Anfield sign, players’ tunnel, dugouts, dressing room, and trophy displays on non-restricted days. Matchday and Legends experiences are bookable separately through the club’s tour system.
facts.best_time: Weekday tour slots for quieter access; Premier League home weekends for Kop atmosphere. Museum-only tickets suit visitors when full stadium tours are sold out.
facts.how_to_get_there: Anfield Road / Walton Breck Road area, Liverpool L4 0TH. Bus corridors from Liverpool city centre (Queen Square / Lime Street); limited nearby parking on matchdays—use park-and-ride or walk from Sandhills / Kirkdale rail where practical.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (liverpoolfc.com / bookings.liverpoolfc.com tour calendar). Street-level landmarks such as the Paisley Gateway and Kop façade are separate exterior stops before the paid tour—photograph them from the pavement; they are not the hero image.

facts.one_liner: Estadio Alberto J. Armando—La Bombonera—Boca Juniors’ steep La Boca bowl.
facts.why_go: Estadio Alberto J. Armando, universally nicknamed La Bombonera (“the chocolate box”), is Boca Juniors’ home at Brandsen 805 in Buenos Aires’ La Boca barrio. The night match photo shows the steep three-tier stands opposite the flat stacked-box side that gives the ground its uneven “D” footprint and intense, close-to-pitch acoustics. Opened in 1940 and renamed for club president Alberto J. Armando in 2000, it remains an active Primera División and continental venue. Museo de la Pasión Boquense runs museum visits and guided Estadio Tours through stands, pitchside areas, and the away dressing room when fixtures allow.
facts.best_time: Weekday museum hours (typically 10:00–18:00, box office to 17:30) for tours; evening Superclásico or Libertadores nights for atmosphere—tickets are scarce. Confirm tour cancellations on training or match days.
facts.how_to_get_there: Brandsen 805, La Boca, CABA. Bus lines along Brandsen / Avenida Almirante Brown; taxi or rideshare from San Telmo / Puerto Madero is common. Arrive early on match days—street closures and bag checks are routine.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (museoboquense.com daily museum/tour offers; Boca first-team calendar active September 2026). Bring DNI/passport for tour entry as required by the museum. The museum does not sell match tickets.

facts.one_liner: Hungary’s national stadium in Zugló; ~67,000 seats; 2026 UCL final host.
facts.why_go: Puskás Aréna in Budapest’s XIV district (Zugló) is Hungary’s national football stadium—the night interior with red seating tiers, open pitch, and steel lattice roof matches the photo. Built on the site of the former Népstadion and opened 15 November 2019, it holds on the order of 67,000 spectators and is named for Ferenc Puskás. It hosts the national team and major UEFA fixtures; on 30 May 2026 it staged the UEFA Champions League final (Paris Saint-Germain beat Arsenal on penalties). The on-site Puskás Museum offers Arena Tours daily at 11:00, 13:30, and 15:00 when scheduled.
facts.best_time: Museum hours Monday–Sunday 10:00–18:00 (last ticket 17:00) for tours; national-team or European nights for a full bowl. Weekday morning tour slots are usually quieter.
facts.how_to_get_there: Istvánmezei út 3–5, 1146 Budapest. M2 (red) metro to Puskás Ferenc Stadion; approach Gate X from Stefánia út or Gate V from Dózsa György út for museum/tour access per visitor info.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN as of 2025–2026 (puskasarenamuzeum.hu visitor info and 2026 UCL final hosted here). Scout swapped Rajko Mitić Stadium → Puskás Aréna. Arena Insight tickets reach stands only; book the full Arena Tour for dressing-room/route access.
